learningObjective: Distinguish the intended uses of FP8 E4M3 and E5M2 formats and their trade-offs.
stem: NVIDIA Hopper Tensor Cores support two FP8 formats: E4M3 (4-bit exponent, 3-bit mantissa) and E5M2 (5-bit exponent, 2-bit mantissa). Which of the following statements about their intended uses and trade-offs are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: E4M3 has narrower dynamic range but higher mantissa precision than E5M2; it is typically preferred for forward-pass activations and weights whose distribution is bounded and needs precision.
E5M2 has wider dynamic range (5-bit exponent) but lower precision; it is typically preferred for gradients during training, whose values span a large magnitude range.
Both formats have the same total bit width (8 bits including sign); the choice affects precision-vs-range, not memory footprint.
Using FP8 requires no scaling factors; the format itself handles the entire dynamic range needed in DNN training.
FP8 kernels are supported on Ampere Tensor Cores at the same throughput as FP16; the format was retroactively enabled on sm_80 via a driver update.

explanation: A and B match the design intent as codified in the NVIDIA / Arm / Intel FP8 whitepaper and Transformer Engine: E4M3 for weights/activations (bounded distributions), E5M2 for gradients (wide dynamic range). C is a straightforward observation: both are 8 bits total. D is false: FP8's dynamic range is small enough that per-tensor or per-block scaling is essential; Transformer Engine automates this via `DelayedScaling`. E is false: FP8 Tensor Cores debuted on Hopper (sm_90); they are not supported on Ampere (sm_80).

optionExplanations.A: Correct: E4M3 use case per NVIDIA/Arm/Intel FP8 spec.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: E5M2 use case per FP8 spec.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: FP8 workflows require per-tensor/block scale factors.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: FP8 Tensor Cores are Hopper (sm_90) and later; not available on Ampere.

assumptions: The FP8 formats refer to the NVIDIA/Arm/Intel 2022 specification.
The workload is a DNN training or inference pipeline on Hopper or later.
nonImplications: Does not imply E4M3 and E5M2 always dominate FP16/BF16 in accuracy — they trade precision for compute throughput.
Does not imply all Hopper GEMMs use FP8 by default — frameworks require explicit opt-in.

distractorRationales.D: Understates the need for scaling factors.
